title: Personal Credit Cards: Credit Limit Increases and Decreases
content:
A cardholder of Personal Credit Cards may ask for a higher or a lower credit limit. Increases are open only on tiers that offer them and only on accounts in good standing; decreases are available at almost any time.

## Increases

Only the cardholder can ask for an increase, and asking requires the cardholder's agreement to a credit inquiry. It is available only on a tier whose waiting period is not shown as not offered. All of the following apply, judged on the bank's records for the account:

- the account is active and is not past due;
- the account has been open for at least the tier's waiting period in whole months; the months are counted as calendar months from the opening date, and the request qualifies on or after the date that lies that many calendar months after opening;
- where the account has had an earlier increase, at least the tier's spacing period in whole months has passed since that increase;
- the new limit exceeds the current limit by no more than the tier's largest increase percentage, does not exceed the tier's highest credit limit, and remains subject to the combined credit line ceiling across the customer's cards.

| Tier | Months open before an increase may be requested | Months between increases | Largest single increase, percent of the current limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | not offered | 6 | not offered |
| College Rewards Visa | 6 | 6 | 25 percent |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 6 | 6 | 100 percent |

Boundary cases (hypothetical dates): an account opened on 14 March qualifies on the waiting-period test from 14 September of the same year onward; a request on 13 September does not qualify.

## Decreases

A decrease asked for by the cardholder may be made at any time on an account that is active or suspended. The floor for the new limit is whichever is larger: the tier's lowest credit limit, or the balance now owed taken up to the next whole hundred dollars.

> Hypothetical illustration: with 2340.15 USD owed, raising that figure to the next whole hundred gives 2400.00 USD; if the tier's lowest limit is below that, the limit cannot be taken under 2400.00 USD.

## Secured Visa

A Secured Visa limit moves only when the security deposit changes, which lies outside these rules.
